question: Safe feature disposition under rare work, dependencies and uncertain demand

proposed_rules.intent: Preserve problem, evidence status and affected actors before feature disposition.
conditions: For a claimed need, separate desired outcome from requested implementation.
Attach observed/reported/assumed/unknown provenance without converting the latter two into evidence.
Before removing a capability, check affected support/operations/dependent-team work as well as front-stage usage.
exceptions: A small, understood edit needs only a proportionate check.
An unknown need does not automatically block unrelated implementation work; hold only the affected irreversible disposition.
proposed_rules.failure: High-volume customer telemetry is mistaken for the complete set of needs and a rare support task disappears.
proposed_rules.test: Brief contains a customer view, a rare support export and an untested feature request; output must preserve support outcome, distinguish request from need, and mark request evidence as unknown.
proposed_rules.novelty: Inherited goal traceability; new explicit affected-actor coverage and proportionality/evidence-status gates.

proposed_rules.intent: Treat removal and consolidation as a coverage transition.
conditions: For a removal proposal, classify each affected need as ended with evidence, continued through a named replacement, or explicitly outside the proposed service scope.
For replacement, record how users reach the successor and which preserved constraints it satisfies.
Flag an unresolved surviving need or broken old entry as a defect, rather than counting fewer features as improvement.
exceptions: A demonstrably obsolete need can end without a successor.
A proposed scope reduction is legitimate if the unmet need and decision are explicit; the Skill must not silently treat it as preserved coverage.
This unit plans IA and capability migration; B/C own transition behavior and data mechanics.
proposed_rules.failure: Two screens merge but one role loses a required operation, or a retired bookmarked destination becomes an unexplained dead end.
proposed_rules.test: Deletion with absent successor fails when a required need survives; obsolete-need evidence permits removal; replacement must cover the role and old-entry disposition.
proposed_rules.novelty: Adds explicit retirement-reason alternatives and legacy-entry transition beyond inherited keep/merge/defer/remove labels.

proposed_rules.intent: Keep uncertain priority decisions reversible and testable.
conditions: Use estimated inputs only with their assumption status visible.
Compare plausible scenarios for the inputs that could reverse the ordering.
If ranking changes across plausible scenarios, record a provisional order and the observation that would resolve it.
Retain hard requirements separately from optional benefit ranking.
exceptions: Do not invent numerical ranges without a basis; qualitative scenarios can expose uncertainty.
Do not require a full economic model for a minor UI choice.
Hard-requirement protection is inherited from prior requirements rules, not established by the benefits article alone.
proposed_rules.failure: An unknown usage estimate becomes zero demand and permanently eliminates a capability; fabricated precision hides a ranking reversal.
proposed_rules.test: Change only an uncertain benefit estimate so the optional ranking reverses; output should expose uncertainty and a revisit condition, while mandatory coverage stays intact.
proposed_rules.novelty: Refines inherited priority rationale with sensitivity and explicit revisit criteria; no new universal score formula.

not_searched: Quantitative controlled experiments for these three composite rules
GOV.UK functional standard full text and healthcare service assessment surfaced in audit query; only snippets seen, not used as sources
next_questions: Can merge-equivalence checks preserve permission/scope and prerequisites without disallowing legitimate shared interfaces?
How should aliases and deprecated destinations preserve findability after taxonomy consolidation?
stopping_reason: Source passages attached to the new operational questions; source guidance has no empirical effectiveness proof, which remains a verification task. This is not saturation.

sources.title: Learning about users and their needs
sources.locator: Researching / Validating user needs; Linking user needs to user stories
sources.claim: Evidence-based needs describe a problem and outcome; implementation-specific user stories remain linked to needs. Research includes support staff and people who have difficulty with the current service.
sources.limits: Official service-design guidance, not a controlled comparison. No prevalence threshold or automatic feature-removal rule is supplied.
sources.publication_safety: Metadata and short quotation only; retained source text stays private.

sources.title: Retiring your service
sources.locator: Consider user needs; Telling your users; Make a plan to redirect traffic
sources.claim: Retirement distinguishes needs that disappear, needs served by a replacement, and needs no longer served by government. Users, direct-entry routes, APIs and assisted channels require transition consideration.
sources.limits: Whole-service retirement guidance. Applying its preservation questions to an individual feature is this campaign’s inference. Government-specific notification and domain-retention rules are not transplanted.
sources.publication_safety: Metadata and short quotation only; retained source text stays private.

sources.title: Measuring the benefits of your service
sources.locator: Discovery; Alpha; Show improvement; Scrutinise your assumptions
sources.claim: Early estimates may use assumptions. A baseline, alternative solutions, delivery costs and sensitivity to uncertain inputs support comparison; metrics and later observations update the model.
sources.limits: Guidance for service investment and benefits. It does not prescribe a feature ranking formula, a numerical confidence threshold, or measured effectiveness for this Skill.

sources.claim: Affected users include support, operations and integrating teams. Trace technical choices to their needs and consider change impacts. Small, well-understood changes warrant lightweight checks.
